description: We are a team of four enthusiastic students participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, is an interactive game that teaches students how to manage a Moon or Mars base. We are interested in space exploration, AI, coding, and game development. We welcome creative and passionate teammates skilled in programming, research, graphics, or design. Beginners are welcome too. Let's explore beyond limits! 🚀
summary: Space Explorer: Build Your Space Colony is an interactive 3D game that challenges players to build and manage a sustainable outpost on the Moon or Mars. Players balance essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, power, fuel, and materials while constructing habitats, greenhouses, medical facilities, and other colony buildings. They can also switch to exploration mode to collect research samples, discover water ice, investigate signals, and repair equipment. The game introduces players to challenges of living beyond Earth, including limited resources, equipment failures, dust storms, and radiation protection. By combining colony management with hands-on exploration, our project makes space settlement concepts engaging and easier to understand.
details:
DSpace Explorer: Build Your Space Colony is an interactive 3D space-colony simulation developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Three.js (r128).

Players begin by customizing an astronaut and choosing Earth, the Moon, or Mars as their destination. In Colony Mode, they construct and manage facilities, including habitats, greenhouses, oxygen generators, water recyclers, solar panels, medical centres, laboratories, garages, and radiation shelters. Each facility has different resource costs and effects.

Players must balance oxygen, water, food, power, fuel, materials, medical supplies, and credits to maintain their colony. In Explore Mode, they navigate the 3D environment, collect research samples, discover water ice, investigate mysterious signals, and repair damaged buildings.

Random events, such as equipment malfunctions, resource shortages, storms, and solar particle events, introduce additional challenges.

The game incorporates educational space-science concepts using a saved snapshot of NASA NSSDCA Planetary Fact Sheets. These resources provide planetary gravity values and information about magnetic fields and Mars's thin atmosphere. Gravity is scaled for simplified gameplay physics. The radiation system uses a fictional 0–100 gameplay scale based on team-created assumptions and does not represent NASA radiation measurements.

The game also features keyboard and touch controls, astronaut customization, missions, resource management, and automatic saving.

Our goal is to make the challenges of planning and maintaining a space outpost understandable through interactive learning. By combining building, exploration, scientific concepts, and problem-solving, we aim to make space education more engaging and accessible.

The Code generation, planning, and debugging were assisted by Claude (Anthropic) and chatgpt, while audio elements were generated through code.
